package.question: Does training a translation model with Method M improve translation quality over supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning baselines, and is the improvement consistent across low- and high-resource target languages and metrics?
package.methods_summary: Method M fine-tunes a neural MT model with two losses at once: cross-entropy on labeled sentence pairs and an 'energy' loss given by the negative score of a reference-free quality estimator (COMET-KIWI) on the model's own sampled translations of unlabeled source sentences; gradients pass through the estimator into the MT model via a straight-through estimator. Method M-static keeps the estimator fixed; Method M-dynamic also updates it contrastively to prefer gold over sampled translations. Two data techniques are added: filtering labeled pairs by estimator score (FILTER) and pairing each labeled batch with similar unlabeled sources (NN). RL baselines (REINFORCE, PPO) use the same estimator score as reward.
package.experimental_setup: MT model: mBART-50 (about 610M parameters, monolingual pretraining only). Data: IWSLT2017 English-German/Chinese (50K pairs sampled) and ML50 English-Bengali, -Azerbaijani, -Mongolian, -Marathi, -Kazakh; one fifth of the pairs are used as labeled data and all source sentences as unlabeled data. Training: 10 epochs with early stopping on validation COMET-KIWI. Metrics: SacreBLEU, COMET-KIWI (reference-free), COMET (reference-based) and XCOMET. Main-table numbers are means over three seeds.

results_tables.caption: English-to-X translation quality on seven target languages (training-set sizes: BN 4K, AZ 5K, MN 7K, MR 9K, KA 12K, DE 50K, ZH 50K sentence pairs). Each value is the average of three runs with different seeds. Method M variants use labeled-data filtering and nearest-neighbour unlabeled batches.
results_tables.notes: Restructured from the source's two main-results tables (low- and high-resource pairs): rows are system x metric, columns are language pairs; values verbatim. COMET-KIWI and XCOMET per-language columns dropped. The source labels Kazakh as 'EN-KA'. Seed means only; no standard deviations or significance tests reported.

results_tables.caption: Results averaged over four target languages (German, Chinese, Bengali, Marathi), including reinforcement-learning baselines that use the same quality estimator as reward. +Mono = the quality-estimator-based loss is also applied to unlabeled (monolingual) source sentences; -Mono = without them.
results_tables.notes: RL baselines were run without the FILTER/NN data techniques. Rows dropped: supervised+FILTER and other Method M data-technique combinations. COMET-KIWI is also the quality estimator used inside training and for early stopping.
